newsitem.title: JAPAN: LTCB SAYS TO CUT DEBENTURE COUPON TO 2.0 PCT.
newsitem.headline: LTCB SAYS TO CUT DEBENTURE COUPON TO 2.0 PCT.

text.p: The Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan Ltd (LTCB) said on Tuesday it would cut the coupon rate of its August five-year bank debenture to 2.0 percent from 2.2 percent in July.
LTCB also said it would leave its long-term prime lending rate for August unchanged from the previous month, at 2.7 percent.

The spread between the coupon rate of the Industrial Bank of Japan's (IBJ) five-year bank debentures and LTCB's debentures is now 0.2 percentage point, the lowest level since January, and down from 0.4 percentage point previously.
LTCB said in a statement that the cut in the coupon rate for its August debentures reflected recent economic and financial trends.
There were no bids or offers for LTCB's July bank debentures with a coupon rate of 2.2 percent on Tuesday.
"There are no bids or offers today, but they have been bid and offered at around two percent recently," a trader at a brokerage house said.
Traders said market yields of LTCB's debentures have declined since the bank announced on July 15 that it would form a strategic alliance with the Swiss Bank Corp.
Bank debentures are the long-term credit banks' main fund-raising tool.

On Monday, the IBJ, Japan's largest long-term credit bank, said it would leave its August long-term prime rate unchanged at 2.7 percent. It also said it would leave the coupon rate for its August five-year debentures unchanged at 1.8 percent.
The prime rate, which is applied to loans of one year and longer to Japanese long-term credit banks' most creditworthy clients, is reviewed every month, reflecting market trends.
